messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Long commands not broken properly (Overfull \hbox)
parts:
If you do not like the automatic formatting, you can turn it off by
tidy=FALSE, and format your code by hand:

<<Test, tidy=FALSE>>=
TestObj1 <- data.frame(Name = factor(c("B", "C", "A")), Bla = rnorm(3))
TestObj2 <- data.frame(Name = factor(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 3)),
Bla = rnorm(9))
TestObj1 <- TestObj1[unlist(lapply(levels(TestObj2$Name),
function(i) which(as.character(TestObj1$Name) == i))), ]
@

http://yihui.name/knitr/options

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Long commands not broken properly (Overfull \hbox)
parts:
It may sound like an easy problem, but actually it requires an update
of R internals. You can either convince R core this is necessary, or
do it by yourself, submit a patch and pray that they could accept it
-- perhaps start from these files:

$ grep do_deparse -r ./ --exclude-dir=.svn
./src/main/names.c://{"deparseRd", do_deparseRd, 0, 11,
2, {PP_FUNCALL, PREC_FN, 0}},
./src/main/names.c:{"deparse", do_deparse, 0, 11, 5, {PP_FUNCALL, PREC_FN, 0}},
./src/main/deparse.c: * Deparsing has 3 layers. The user interface,
do_deparse, should
./src/main/deparse.c:* takes a cutoff value as a parameter. Then
"do_deparse" and "deparse1"
./src/main/deparse.c:SEXP attribute_hidden do_deparse(SEXP call, SEXP
op, SEXP args, SEXP rho)
./src/include/Internal.h:SEXP do_deparse(SEXP, SEXP, SEXP, SEXP);
./src/library/tools/src/gramRd.y:/* "do_deparseRd"
./src/library/tools/src/gramRd.c:/* "do_deparseRd"
./src/gnuwin32/Rdll.hide: do_deparse

But I would argue that whenever you see three braces in one place or a
line of more than 80 characters, you probably need to reconsider how
to organize your code. In your case, adding {} to your function will
help a lot.

There are many coding styles on the web, e.g.
https://github.com/hadley/devtools/wiki/Style

Regards,

Frankly speaking, I do not follow everything in these coding styles
(but max 80 chars per line is a good one), and I do not like the way
how R parser breaks the lines either (e.g. it often breaks ] into the
next line). You are right that it can be a good idea for formatR to
improve it, but it does not have high priority for me (i.e. please
feel free to send me pull requests on Github), nor do I really know
what is a good rule to break a line like the one in your case.
